findings.summary: the `optional` data sink compiled its initializer TWICE -- once as a value, once falling through to the inner sink -- so scene 173's `WireMesh[] | null` built its twelve wireframe tubes twice and the native scene drew 56 meshes against the browser's 44, at 0.000 parity only because the duplicates were exactly co-located; the handle arm beside it already carried the reason and now covers every inner type

the whole nullable-handle and handle-rebind slice emitted nothing: both scenes register at their own `?freeze=1` pose, which folds away the branch that clears, guards, removes and re-points. Rather than delete a mechanism the corpus does reach one branch deeper, a project-owned gate now removes an obstacle from a plain statement -- `regression-nav-obstacles`, 0.000 both backends, with the two computed routes visibly different so a removal that did nothing would show

the nullable obstacle was a second answer to a question `nullableResourceKind` + `optionalStorageCpp` already answers with `std::optional`, and `emitOptionalResourceAssignment` warns against exactly that conflation by name; the obstacle joins that lane and the parallel zero-handle representation is gone

`handleValueKinds` was a fourth registry of which value kinds are handles, disagreeing with `isHandleKind` and with its own doc; the rebind keys on `isHandleKind`, which is what the data model means by a copyable handle

which build arm runs was stated twice -- proved at generation, then re-derived at run time by the emitted `create_nav_mesh` -- and the tile-cache PAL half plus its third-party library linked into every navigation scene including the four that cannot take that arm; generation's answer now reaches the build as `navigation:tile-cache`, so a solo scene emits no tile-cache call, carries none of the obstacle surface, compiles none of the PAL half and links none of the library

the two RecastDemo files were installed as sources and compiled by the consumer, which is the only third-party translation unit inside the project target and dragged in a project-wide C language, a `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` pin, a sticky cache key that would have wiped all 194 existing build trees (~2.4 CPU-hours of recompilation), and an unguarded `/W0;/fp:strict` that would reach gcc as a filename on Linux; the overlay port builds them into a library of their own instead

`tileCacheGeneratorConfigDefaults`' three numbers were baked past the drift gate that exists for exactly them, and disagreed across the layer boundary -- the emitted dispatch read an absent `maxObstacles` as solo while the PAL read it as 128; `expectedLayersPerTile` joins the gate and the other two stop carrying defaults, because the arm is SELECTED by them

the PAL returned `std::optional` from both obstacle factories only for the generated wrapper to turn `nullopt` into a throw one frame later, where every other failure in that PAL throws directly; it throws with the wrapper's own spelling and the optional is gone from two signatures and two rethrow blocks

each obstacle entry point resolved and validated the plugin, then called `navigation_update_obstacles` which resolved and validated it again; the three share one `drain_obstacle_requests` over the state they already hold

`RecastOwner` hand-rolled `std::unique_ptr` -- deleted copy, move ctor, move assign, reset, destructor -- in a file that already spells that idiom three times with a function-pointer deleter, and left both idioms side by side in one struct

the tile-cache arm re-copied three blocks the solo arm already had after the branch's own factoring stopped short: the geometry preamble, the `fail` lambda and the query-init tail, the last two encoding the same 2048-node budget and filter install twice

`rasterize_tile_layers` was a 121-line lambda that pushed the two-pass loop which IS `generateTileCache`'s shape 120 lines below its setup, and made ten per-tile early returns read as returns from the build; it is a named function beside the others

`staticZeroOrPositive` was a fourth private copy of static-number reading, weaker than the shared one: it accepted only a bare numeric literal, so `maxObstacles: MAX_OBSTACLES` refused where `compileStaticNumber` folds it

`rebindVariable` re-derived the symbol resolution `defineVariable` performs and walked the scope array a third way (copying it per rebind), so one error string appeared four times and three walks had to stay in step; both are shared helpers now

`agent_goto` still hand-built the `NavVec3` the branch's own `nav_vec3` helper exists for; `rebindingScopeDepth` was a number used only as a boolean with a stated purpose it did not implement; the build-arm truth table was split by an unrelated refusal; one paragraph of reasoning was written twice; `statements.ts` imported from `./types.js` twice
